title: Rounding Forecast
summary: Predict how R rounds and formats numbers, and why APA write-ups use formatC() rather than round().
hints: `round()` returns a number, and R prints numbers without trailing zeros. `formatC(..., format = "f")` returns text with exactly the digits you ask for.
R rounds a 5 to the even digit (IEC 60559), so `round(2.5)` and `round(1.5)` both give 2.
`sub("^0", "", x)` deletes a 0 only at the very start of the text.

quiz.explain: R rounds halves to the even digit, the IEC 60559 standard. It rarely matters in a report, but now it won't surprise you.

quiz.prompt: A mean of 3.10 should be reported as 3.10. What does `round()` give?
quiz.explain: `round()` returns a number, and numbers print without trailing zeros. APA wants two decimals shown, so `round()` alone isn't enough for a write-up.
`formatC(format = "f")` returns text with exactly `digits` decimals, trailing zeros kept. That's the one for reports.

quiz.prompt: A p-value or a correlation can't be bigger than 1, so APA drops the leading zero. What does this give?
quiz.explain: `formatC()` makes "0.046" and `sub("^0", "", ...)` removes the 0 at the start. (A negative r needs `sub("^(-?)0", "\\1", x)` to keep its minus sign.)
`big.mark` adds a thousands separator; APA uses commas in numbers of 1,000 or more.

quiz.prompt: SPSS shows Sig. = .000. What does this code give for p = .00002?
quiz.explain: A p-value is never exactly 0. APA reports anything below .001 as *p* < .001, so a formatter needs that special case.
